hypotheses_verdict.decisive_falsifier: Signature selection rule strictly forbids Delta I = 2 stretched E2 interband decay (Delta alpha = 0) for 1-phonon wobbling. Experimentally, 3 strong stretched E2 transitions (871.2, 994.3, 1108 keV) directly connect Band 4 and Band 1.

Band 1 is a 1-quasiparticle nu h11/2 configuration. In 1-quasiparticle systems, single-particle momentum j and core rotation R span a 2D plane (scalar triple product j.(R x axis) = 0), precluding a non-planar chiral geometry.

Normal-deformed Band 1 (Qt = 2.58 eb) and Band 4 exhibit strong discrete mutual decay branches without the high-barrier tunneling hindrance characteristic of shape coexistence. Shape coexistence exists in 131Ce only as an unlinked highly deformed (HD) band (Q0 = 7.3 eb).

A pure single-quasiparticle signature partner band decays primarily through Delta I = 1 M1 transitions. It cannot account for the three strong Delta I = 2 stretched E2 interband branches (871.2, 994.3, 1108 keV) whose branching ratios reach 64% of in-band transitions.

Naturally explains the coexistence of both Delta I = 2 stretched E2 transitions (Alaga rule component from K_0 + 2 to K_0) and Delta I = 1 mixed transitions. Completely consistent with the gamma-soft core 130Ce (S(4) < 0) and Alwaleedi Table 5.3 assignment.

conclusion: Bands 1 and 4 in 131Ce are unambiguously decoupled from wobbling and chirality. Band 4 is established as a gamma-vibrational phonon coupled to the nu h11/2 quasiparticle (gamma (x) nu h11/2), coexisting with normal rotation in a gamma-soft nuclear core.
